scope: Reference-only correction owned by this review: two stale positive source references in the C3 network targeting specification. No product code, roadmap, inventory, task, or product validation files were changed.
preexistingWorktreeNote: The specification already contained unrelated reference repairs when this task began. Those edits were preserved. This task added exactly two source-reference replacements.

replacements.reason: The C3 master-destruction requirement is implemented by destroyC3Unit. Its master-slave branch removes the complete network when the destroyed member has role master.

sourceEvidence.mapping: Lines 105-112 document destruction behavior; lines 114-117 define destroyC3Unit; lines 128-130 remove the full master-slave network for a destroyed master; lines 133-149 remove a non-master member or dissolve a one-member remainder.
The C3 module barrel exports destroyC3Unit from ./state, confirming the corrected implementation is the public C3 state API.

replacements.reason: The repository's canonical C3 catalog is under public/data/equipment/official/electronics, and the old data/equipment/electronics path is absent.

sourceEvidence.mapping: ElectronicsCategory.C3 is the canonical C3 System category.
Canonical display names map to catalog IDs c3-master, c3-slave, and c3i.
The official equipment index registers electronics/c3.json as the c3 electronics file.
The official loader reads indexed electronics files and converts each item into the electronics lookup map.
The catalog contains c3-master (lines 8-21), c3-slave (lines 24-37), and c3i / Improved C3 Computer (lines 40-53), including the specified weights and critical slots.

limits: This is a source-reference and path correction only; no product tests, build, browser proof, or runtime behavior validation was requested or run.

The evidence proves the replacement targets resolve through the current C3 state implementation and official catalog index/loader chain. It does not prove every catalog consumer or the full C3 gameplay contract.
The source line mappings are anchored to the captured live files and their recorded SHA-256 hashes; future edits may move line numbers.
